figureObjective: Compare conduction, convection, and radiation by carrier and material-medium requirement under a temperature difference.

claims.text: Heat transfer occurs by conduction, convection, and radiation, and the modes may occur simultaneously.
Conduction transfers heat through direct physical contact.
Convection transfers heat through the movement of a liquid or gas.
Radiation transfers heat through emitted or absorbed electromagnetic radiation and requires no material medium.
With a temperature difference, net heat transfer proceeds from the higher-temperature region to the lower-temperature region.
